lines.en: It is said that strong communities are built not on money, but on trust between neighbors.
What holds a family together is not the absence of conflict, but the willingness to forgive.
The longer a friendship lasts, the more it teaches us about patience and acceptance.
Not until we lose touch with old friends do we realize how much they meant to us.
However busy life becomes, we should never be too busy for the people we love.
It is often the smallest act of kindness that a person remembers for the rest of their life.
Were people to listen more and judge less, most conflicts would disappear within minutes.
Little things, repeated daily, matter more in a relationship than grand gestures made once a year.
What modern life has taken from us is the time to simply sit with one another and talk.
Rarely do we thank the people who shaped us until it is almost too late.
What neighbors remember years later is not the gifts, but the times you simply showed up.
It is in difficult times, not easy ones, that you discover who your real friends are.
The more connected we become online, the lonelier many people say they feel.
Were families to eat one meal together every day, many small misunderstandings would disappear.
Not only should we apologize when we are wrong, but we should also forgive when others are.
